scope: Make task operation versions stable during scheduler/progress updates while preserving input, generation, phase, terminal-state, authorization and transactional action conflicts

original_finding.condition: Actual history worker returned JobSnooze(500ms) while the persisted child run remained waiting_parent; scheduler fields invalidated the full-row hash

operation_version_semantics.wire_contract: Existing Task.version and TaskAction.expected_version strings; all protected contract files unchanged
operation_version_semantics.queue_state: available/scheduled/pending/running share the active operation class; retryable/discarded/cancelled/completed remain distinct; recorded retryable/discarded error history is included
operation_version_semantics.analysis: Preserve run/task/candidate generation, selected definition versions, actual/captured snapshot ids and hashes, input hash, parent relation, initial-state resolution, resources, errors and meaningful business stage. Cursor/progress/updated timestamp/document version/accumulated final state are excluded.
operation_version_semantics.recompute: Preserve task/replay identity, fixed requested/replay interval, device/definition, phase/status/reason/error. Progress/cursor/document version are excluded.
operation_version_semantics.pending_and_running: Pending and running in the same captured operation share the active business stage. Pending unresolved children with a parent share the waiting_parent stage, excluding the generated waiting message.
operation_version_semantics.parent_completion: Parent-only updates leave the child confirmation valid while the child remains durably waiting. Saving the resolved child snapshot and beginning execution changes the operation version.

internal_revision.update: Increment once per successful cancel or retry in the same business/Task/River/audit transaction

operation_version_semantics.locking: Existing authorization collection/object shared guards precede linked business object lock, task advisory lock and PostgreSQL River row FOR UPDATE. Latest committed business cursor and results are read within this transaction and preserved on cancellation.
conflicts_retained: prior manual operation or retry generation

verification.atomicity: A failing audit trigger leaves business status/version, sf_tasks.cancelled_ms and internal operation revision unchanged; dropping the trigger allows the original confirmation to succeed with one signed audit entry
verification.parent_and_metadata_competition: One barrier permits actual parent snapshot resolution before stale cancellation (409); another holds the worker after its waiting read while the parent completes and cancellation commits, then lets the old worker merge snooze metadata. No child step commits and the internal revision/trace remain present.
verification.concurrent_confirmations: Two actual HTTP cancellations with the same confirmation produce one 200 and one 409, one cancel audit and revision 1 on both stores
verification.running_progress_fixture: The actual evaluator and commit path run between a test-only 100ms observation delay after each committed step, keeping a finite 80-input run active during the 3s confirmation. Production worker snooze and timeout settings are unchanged.
verification.counting: Top-level and leaf counts are separate. The ordinary run has 82 top-level passes/23 skips and 133 leaf passes/34 skips; the PostgreSQL wrapper has 11 individually skipped children when no DSN is provided. Those 11 execute and pass in both dedicated PostgreSQL runs.
